In line with the July 26, 2017 FOMC statement, incoming data point to continued labor-market strengthening and moderate real activity, while 12-month inflation runs below the 2 percent objective. A forward-looking, expectations-centric approach remains appropriate: with market-based inflation compensation low and longer-term expectations little changed, a gradual, credibility-preserving policy path supports convergence to the symmetric 2 percent goal without inviting time-inconsistency or inflation-bias concerns. The planned, cautious start to balance-sheet normalization—while maintaining reinvestments for now—appropriately limits potential adverse credit-supply effects.

Incorporating the Financial Stability Report perspective, financial vulnerabilities are moderate overall but feature important pockets of risk: asset valuation pressures are elevated amid compressed risk premiums and low term premiums; business debt risks have risen, even as household leverage appears contained; and core funding risks remain low given strong bank capital and liquidity. These conditions argue for continued gradualism to avoid amplifying vulnerabilities or prompting abrupt repricing, and they modestly temper the otherwise positive macro tone.

Bottom line: Growth and employment prospects remain cautiously positive, but elevated valuation pressures and higher corporate leverage flagged in the FSR warrant a slightly more guarded stance than a purely macro read would imply.
